utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone in this courtroom and those who are assisting us just outside this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-00-39-PT, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Krajisnik, can you hear me in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your words, because your microphone was not on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can follow the proceedings in a language I understand. That is being interpreted to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Krajisnik. May I have the appearances for the Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours, counsel. My name is Mark Harmon. To my right is Mr. Alan Tieger. We represent the Office of the Prosecutor in these proceedings. To my left is the case manager, Carmela Annink-Javier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harmon. And for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honours, Nicholas Stewart of the bar of England and Wales. On my right, my co-counsel, Ms. Chrissa Loukas of the New South Wales bar, and on my left, assisting us, Ms. Tatjana Cmeric of the Belgrade bar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stewart. We are here in the beginning of this afternoon for the Pre-Trial Conference. To be more precise, for the second Pre-Trial Conference, because the first Pre-Trial Conference was held already on the 14th of November, 2002. But due to the changes in the Defence team, there is another Pre-Trial Conference scheduled for the beginning of this afternoon. The main reason why the Chamber wanted to have another Pre-Trial Conference is that during the recent 65 ter meetings we had, Mr. Krajisnik was not present in person, and the Chamber would like him to give an opportunity to be updated, as far as he was not already briefed by Defence counsel, and to give him an opportunity to say whatever he'd like to say before the trial starts later this afternoon. Perhaps I give just a very brief history of the case. Mr. Krajisnik, you were arrested in March 2000 and you were transferred to the Tribunal the 3rd of April, 2000. Your Initial Appearance took place on the 7th of April of that same year. Your trial will be held on the basis of the amended, consolidated indictment of the 7th of March, 2002, in which you were charged with genocide, crimes against humanity, and violation of the laws and customs of war, for acts you allegedly have committed while you were serving, among others, as president of the Bosnian Serb Assembly in the Republika Srpska. The trial was scheduled to start already early May 2003, but it was deferred. It was adjourned due to the circumstance that Defence counsel could not function any more. The Chamber once again wants to express its regrets that we cannot start this trial but after nine months of the original date scheduled for it. We have recently discussed what I could call the Rules of the Road, that is, the guidance for the parties how to submit evidence during trial, and other practical matters. Mr. Krajisnik, I take it that Defence counsel has to the extent necessary explained this to you what has been discussed. I see you're nodding yes. One of the problems with transcripts is that it doesn't take any nodding. Therefore, I don't mind that you nod, but I will therefore for the transcript say aloud what I see at the very moment.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My Defence team has informed me about the meeting with you, Your Honour, and I'm sufficiently informed in order to be able to follow everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Krajisnik. Is there any further submission or comment to make on what we discussed earlier in respect of these Rules of the Road? I do understand that the matter of prenumbering of exhibits has been slightly changed, on the request of the Registry. The parties are aware of that, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We have no additional submissions, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Nor we, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Stewart. We also discussed, Mr. Krajisnik, at one of these earlier meetings, that the Prosecution was granted 450 hours to present its case in chief, and that is exclusive of cross-examination. The trial, to start with, will run four days a week for the first two weeks. Then we'll sit for five days a week during the then-coming two weeks, and then I take it that will be the end of February or the very first days of March, we'll postpone the continuance of the trial until the 13th of April of this year. As far as this schedule is concerned, is there any further submission to be made? I see nodding no from all sides, if I'm well informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, in light of the 65 ter conference information that we received that the Prosecution would be limited to 450 hours in its case in chief, we went back and re-calculated the witnesses and the time that we had projected ourselves for what was necessary to present our case. As a result of those calculations, we have eliminated one of the witnesses entirely who we intended to call during this first period of time. So I can provide that information, and I will provide that information to the Defence and to the legal officer. But we are now not intending to call one of the witnesses whom we had previously identified to the Court and to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. I take it, then, that you'll give the name of the witness you withdraw from your list both to the Chamber and to the Defence. Any submissions from the Defence in this respect?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stewart. Then there are still a few motions pending, which ask for some time for us to prepare a decision. These motions regard the admission of a number of witness statements under Rule 92 bis and of adjudicated facts, and I meanwhile received the response of the Defence on the adjudicated facts motion. I also saw that you reserved your right to respond, especially in the adjudicated facts, since they were not translated in B/C/S. I was informed that, at the end of last week, some discussions have been going on between the Registry and the Defence on how to get these translated because these were mainly little quotes from other judgements of Trial Chambers. And I also did understand that finally a solution has been reached on that issue. Is that correct, Mr. Stewart?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stewart. Any further submissions to be made in respect of the pending motions? I see that neither of the parties gets on his feet, so therefore, I take it that no submissions are to be made. The last point on my agenda, Mr. Krajisnik, concerns you more personally. Is there any submission to be made in respect of your present health situation?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wonder whether the Tribunal should go into private session for this particular item, or closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you'd prefer to deal with the personal health situation of the accused in private session, then we'll turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, we would prefer that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.
